2. Facts leading to this rule, in brief, are that the petitioner was the proprietor of a firm named, M/s. Bangladesh Decorators situated in Barisal and carried on the business of supply of tables, chairs, utensils etc. on hire. On 30-1-76 a letter purported to have been issued by the Deputy Commissioner, Bakarganj and signed by someone on behalf of the Deputy Commissioner was served upon the petitioner directing him not to wake any contract for supplying furniture on hire to anybody without the written permission from the Deputy Commissioner's office. A Photostat copy of the said letter has been annexed to the petition as annexure B. Thereafter, on 11-2-76 a peon of the office of the Nazarat Deputy Collector, Barisal came to the petitioner in the office of his business firm and asked him to see the Nazarat Deputy Collector immediately. The petitioner accordingly went to him but was rebuked by the said officer who asked his staff to take the petitioner to the Sub. Divisional Magistrate Sader, South, Barisal. There, the petitioner found that a complaint has already been lodged against him by the Deputy Commissioner. On the basis of the said complaint the Sub-Divisional Magistrate took cognizance of the alleged offence sunder sections 186 and 174 of' the Penal Code and C.R. Case No. 98 of 1976 was started against the accused petitioner and he was immediately sent to jail custody. The petitioner on the following day prayed for bail but the same was rejected and thereafter the petitioner moved the learned sessions Judge who granted him bail, the certified copy of the order has been annexed to the petition as annexure E. The petitioner-thereafter moved this court for quashing and obtained the present rule. 

 3. We have heard the learned Advocate in support of the rule and have perused the records of the case. The petitioner has been charged under sections 174 and 186 of the Penal Code. Now section 174 of the Penal Code reads as follow:- 

 Section 186 which deals with obstructing a public servant in discharging his public functions reads as follow:- 

 "Section 186. Whoever voluntarily obstructs any public servant in the discharge of his  public functions shall be punished With imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both. 

 5. Under section 174 of the Penal Code non-attendance in obedience to an order from public servant is punishable only when the said order was a legal order and was issued by a public servant legally competent to issue the same. There is nothing in the petition of complaint to show that any legal order was served on the petitioner nor f r that matter we find that the Nazarat Deputy Collector had any legal authority to summon the petitioner, Section 186 of the Penal Code which deals with the obstruction of a public servant in the discharge of his public duties, shows that the obstruction must be voluntary and the said obstruction must be in relation to a public servant who was discharging his public functions, The allegation in the petition of complaint was that certain chairs were requisitioned for the purpose of exhibition held at Barisal Town and the petitioner had refused to supply the same. But there is nothing on record to show that there was any such requisition. On the contrary, the petitioner has annexed to this petition "Annexure F", a letter from the Additional Deputy Commissioner who was the General Secretary of the Exhibition Comimittee dated14-2-76 requesting him to supply 1000 chairs for the said exhibition which request was duly complied with. We are, therefore, satisfied that the petition of complaint does not disclose any offence either under section 174 or under section 186 of the Penal Code and further prolongation of the prosecution against the petitioners would be sheer abuse of the process of the court and unnecessary harassment to the assused petitioner.
